title: Paginating a GraphQL query with gh api --paginate --slurp
answers: how to paginate gh api graphql query
gh api graphql paginate slurp jq
gh api graphql all pages jq shape
body:
Use `gh api graphql --paginate --slurp -f query=...` to fetch every page of a cursor-based connection into one call.
--slurp wraps all pages in a single JSON array, so the jq must iterate `.[].data.repository...` rather than read one page's object.
The query must declare a `$endCursor: String` variable, pass `after: $endCursor` on the connection, and select `pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor }`; gh uses these to follow pages.
In .github/workflows/rerun-workflow-run.yml, variables are passed with `-f owner= -f name= -f sha=`, and the `object(expression: $sha)` lookup resolves the head SHA to a Commit.

search: To paginate cursor-based GraphQL queries inside GitHub Actions workflow steps, execute gh api graphql with --paginate and --slurp. The --slurp flag wraps responses in a single JSON array requiring jq to iterate .[].data.repository, while the GraphQL query must declare $endCursor: String, pass after: $endCursor, and select pageInfo with hasNextPage and endCursor. In .github/workflows/rerun-workflow-run.yml, parameters are supplied with -f owner=, -f name=, and -f sha= to resolve head commits using object(expression: $sha).
